There's no way to make a sweeping statement about it, since everyone has their reasons. I support doctor-assisted suicide, for example. But I sometimes view suicide as selfish, depending on the circumstances.

A few years ago, my step-grandmother's partner, let's call him Roger, committed suicide after being diagnosed with Parkinson's. The disease had not progressed very far by then, but he did it anyway, with no warning to anyone.

He did this knowing that my step-grandmother's previous husband had also committed suicide. (He had untreated depression.)

I firmly believe that if Roger had spoken to step-grandma about wanting to end it all, she would have supported him in his decision. But I also think she would have made him wait longer than he did, and he probably didn't want that. So, he purposely chose to break her heart instead, the way her dead husband did. I therefore viewed Roger's suicide as a 100% selfish act and I'm still not sure I've forgiven him for the hurt he caused everyone in this family, especially step-grandma. But, I have to admit that I always thought he was a bit of a dick, so maybe it was my preexisting dislike for him that has shaped my view about what he did. I've never really discussed it with anyone in the family to see what they think, though, because I don't want to dredge up all the pain again. It was bad enough already when he died.
